title: SpiceJet Delhi-Pune Flight Turns Into 'Gas Chamber' as AC Fails, Over 100 Passengers Refuse to Fly
excerpt: Passengers reported being unable to breathe as cabin temperatures soared on the grounded aircraft, forcing it back to the bay in the latest of several AC failures on SpiceJet flights this year.
body:
• Passengers on a SpiceJet flight from Delhi to Pune refused to fly after the air conditioning failed before takeoff, with over 100 flyers demanding to deboard as cabin temperatures soared
  • The aircraft had to return to the parking bay after passengers described the cabin as a "gas chamber" and said they could not breathe in the rising heat
  • The incident is the latest in a string of AC failures on SpiceJet flights this year, raising fresh questions about the budget carrier's fleet maintenance

A SpiceJet flight from Delhi to Pune descended into chaos before it could even take off after the aircraft's air conditioning system failed, leaving passengers in sweltering conditions they described as a "gas chamber." More than 100 passengers refused to fly, forcing the aircraft to return to the parking bay at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport, according to multiple reports from NDTV, India Today, and the Times of India.

Passengers Say They Could Not Breathe

As the aircraft sat on the ground with its AC non-functional, cabin temperatures climbed rapidly in the August heat. Passengers reported struggling to breathe as conditions inside the aircraft became unbearable. "Could not breathe," passengers told the Telegraph India, describing the experience as suffocating.

The situation escalated when furious passengers took their protest to the tarmac, with India Today reporting scenes of passengers confronting airline staff on the ground. The flight was halted before takeoff and returned to the bay after a majority of passengers refused to continue the journey under those conditions.

A Pattern of AC Failures

This is not the first time SpiceJet has faced passenger revolts over non-functioning air conditioning. In July, a Delhi-Pune SpiceJet flight (SG939) was cancelled after a six-hour delay due to a technical fault, stranding over 180 passengers at IGI Airport. Passengers on that flight alleged the airline failed to provide food, water, or clear updates during the ordeal, according to the Daily Jagran.

Earlier in July, another SpiceJet flight at Delhi saw its AC fail during boarding, leading to two passengers being offloaded after they argued with crew and attempted to approach the front galley. In a separate incident, passengers on a Delhi-Darbhanga flight endured over an hour without air conditioning amid a severe heatwave, with cabin temperatures reportedly exceeding 40 degrees Celsius.

The recurring failures have drawn scrutiny from India's aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), which has sought detailed reports on several incidents. Under the DGCA's unruly passenger framework, disrupting a flight can lead to flying bans of up to two years — but aviation experts note that the root cause often lies in operational failures rather than passenger behavior.

SpiceJet's Fleet Challenges

The budget carrier has been working to rebuild its fleet after years of financial turbulence. In late July, SpiceJet announced the induction of three Airbus A320 aircraft under damp lease arrangements, with Chief Business Officer Debojo Maharshi saying the airline was "steadily building capacity ahead of the busy travel season." The airline said it was in advanced discussions with other lessors to add more aircraft in the coming months.

But the AC incidents suggest that fleet expansion alone may not address underlying maintenance and operational challenges, particularly during India's brutal summer months when ground temperatures at Delhi airport can exceed 50 degrees Celsius.

What Travelers Should Know

For passengers flying through Delhi and other North Indian airports during peak summer, AC failures are an increasingly common hazard on budget carriers. Under DGCA regulations, airlines are required to provide basic amenities including water and food during extended delays. Passengers who experience unsafe conditions have the right to demand deplaning and can file formal complaints with the DGCA through its AirSewa portal.

SpiceJet had not issued a detailed statement on the latest incident at the time of reporting.
